m.title: Secondary Storage · worked example
m.q: A photographer carries equipment between locations. Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of choosing an SSD instead of an HDD. [4 marks]
st: The drive will travel often and hold large files.
SSD has no moving parts and is more resistant to impacts; access can also be faster.
An SSD may cost more per GB than an HDD; justify one trade-off. [4]

w: Choose storage for a large, low-cost archive that is rarely moved. Explain your choice. [4]
Magnetic HDD is suitable [1] for high capacities [1] at relatively low cost per GB [1]; slower access may be acceptable for infrequent use [1].
A school sends files on DVDs. Identify the technology and explain a limitation. [3]
Optical storage [1]; the disc is read using a laser [1] and may have limited capacity compared with modern SSDs or HDDs [1].
Explain why an SSD might be suitable for a moving laptop. [3]
No moving parts [1] improves resistance to shocks [1], and fast read/write times [1] suit regular use.
wSteps: Magnetic HDD is suitable [1] for high capacities [1] at relatively low cost per GB [1]; slower access may be acceptable for infrequent use [1].
Optical storage [1]; the disc is read using a laser [1] and may have limited capacity compared with modern SSDs or HDDs [1].
No moving parts [1] improves resistance to shocks [1], and fast read/write times [1] suit regular use.

k.q: Predict the number of 500 MB files that fit in 2000 MB.
k.code:
capacityMB = 2000
fileMB = 500
files = capacityMB DIV fileMB
print(files)
p: Extend to calculate remaining MB using MOD.
k.a: Prints 4, then 5. Remaining MB = capacityMB MOD fileMB (0 in both cases).

r: Why can heavy use of virtual memory make a computer slower? [2]
Pages move between RAM and secondary storage [1], which is slower to access than RAM [1].
What is the purpose of RAM? [1]
To hold programs and data currently in use [1].
State one job performed by the CPU's control unit. [1]
It coordinates and controls instructions/operations, including sending control signals [1].
A program needs 9 GB of working memory but only 6 GB of RAM is free. Calculate the shortage and explain a possible performance effect if the OS uses virtual memory. [3]
Shortage = 9 - 6 = 3 GB [1]. Virtual memory stores some pages on secondary storage [1], which is slower than RAM and may reduce performance [1].

priorExam.q: Explain why virtual memory can allow programs to remain open yet reduce a computer's performance. [3]
priorExam.a: The operating system uses secondary storage for memory pages when RAM is insufficient [1]; moving/accessing those pages takes time [1] because secondary storage is slower than RAM [1].

challenge.coreHint: Use DIV for the number of whole files; ignore partial files.

stretch.task: Change capacityMB to 2300. Predict how many whole 500 MB files fit and use MOD to print remaining space.
stretch.answer: 4 whole files fit, with 300 MB left: 2300 DIV 500 = 4; 2300 MOD 500 = 300.

mastery.task: Extend the original program to calculate the number of whole files and unused storage for capacities of 2300 MB and 2500 MB. Explain why the same number of files may not imply the same unused space.
mastery.hint: Use DIV for the count and MOD for remainder. Compare both outputs.
mastery.answer: For 2300 MB, 4 files fit and 300 MB remains; for 2500 MB, 5 files fit and 0 MB remains. The capacity is not always an exact multiple of the file size. Real drives have filesystem overhead.
